newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil cenbank sees debt-GDP ratio edging up in 96.
newsitem.headline: Brazil cenbank sees debt-GDP ratio edging up in 96.

text.p: Brazil's debt-to-GDP ratio may grow to 36-37 percent in 1996, up from 33 percent in 1995, but is under control, the Central Bank's international affairs director said.
"To say that is explosive or a threat to the Real (Plan to stabilize the economy) is an exaggeration," Franco was quoted as saying by newspaper Estado de Sao Paulo.
"I admit that it is a subject that worries us and our aim is to stabilize it or make it grow more slowly. But we are starting from a low base and with a small increase," Franco said.
Brazil's net public sector debt in June was equivalent to 33.9 percent of GDP, with net internal debt of 210.7 billion reais reaching 29.6 percent of GDP.
Last week, IMF director Vito Tanzi and the Inter- American Development Bank's chief economist Ricardo Hausmann warned that Brazil's growing debt represented the biggest risk to economic stability.

Franco said the concerns were not new to the Brazilian govenment. "We don't need any Dr. Tanzis coming to warn us because since the start of the Real, over two years ago, our aim has been to attack the fiscal question."

Plans to solve the $22-billion debt burden of the banks owned by Brazil's state governments and to securitize an estimated $50-billion black hole in the federal FCVS housing fund would have a "statistical" effect, he said.
"They're debts that already exist, right? It's a question of securitizing them ... That's when they start to appear in the statistics," Franco said.
